title: I3.12 — Semantic Relation Ablation and Raw-Evidence MDSG
objective: Does the MDSG/R1 advantage survive when support/contradiction relations are not handed to the controller?
research_question: Does MDSG/R1 still help when support/contradiction edges are not given for free?
what_is_new_in_i3_12: The only new capability is the upstream semantic-relation layer. MDSG, T2, R1, A1, prompts, utility, and model config are not modified.

S0_oracle_structured.description: Current benchmark condition. Evidence items carry explicit supports/contradicts fields.
S0_oracle_structured.purpose: Reference / upper-bound symbolic condition. S0 regression must reproduce prior behavior.

S1_raw_proposition.description: Controller sees only proposition text. A frozen semantic relation extractor infers SUPPORT/CONTRADICT/NEUTRAL relations.
S1_raw_proposition.purpose: Test whether MDSG/R1 advantage survives when relations are derived, not given.
S1_raw_proposition.controller_sees: proposition text only; relations are inferred by frozen extractor
S1_raw_proposition.critical_constraint: A1, M3, and R1 must receive exactly the same inferred relation graph. Never A1=raw, M3=structured.

S2_semantic_stress.description: Raw propositions with harder semantics: paraphrases, negation, temporal qualifiers, partial support, multi-hop, irrelevant, ambiguous, conflicting sources.
S2_semantic_stress.purpose: Test robustness to realistic semantic uncertainty. Only after S1 passes.

primary_comparison.question: H1: E[U_R1_raw - U_A1_raw] > 0, where both systems operate on the same automatically inferred semantic relation graph.
primary_comparison.estimand: per-task mean utility, bootstrap over tasks

secondary_criteria.rescues: R1 rescues > R1 breaks vs A1
secondary_criteria.steps: Steps_R1_raw < Steps_M3_raw (if M3 retained as comparison arm)

extractor_constraints.hard_fail_if_supplied: extractor must raise if any forbidden field is supplied

information_parity: A1, M3, and R1 must share: same extractor, same relation outputs, same extraction timing, same confidence threshold, same errors. Never A1=raw evidence, M3=structured relation graph.

architecture.flow: Raw propositions -> Frozen semantic relation extractor -> Controller-visible relation graph -> A1 / M3 / R1
architecture.snapshot_still_presents: supports, contradicts to A1/M3/R1 (inferred, not oracle)
architecture.gold_relations: Stored evaluator-side only, never enter controller packets
architecture.separation: Runtime flow (raw -> extractor -> inferred graph -> controller) and evaluator flow (gold graph -> relation scoring) are physically separated

qualification_gates_for_s1.G02: zero evaluator leakage (extractor cannot access gold relations, correct_hypothesis_id, verify_result, expected_terminal, oracle_path)

extractor_identity.description: The extractor is scientifically part of the treatment. Hash: extractor source, relation schema, normalization rules, prompt if LLM-based, model/version if LLM-based, thresholds, hypothesis serializer, evidence serializer.

provenance_lineage.description: Every controller decision traceable: raw evidence text -> hash -> relation extractor -> relation output -> hash -> snapshot -> hash -> MDSG state -> T2 -> representation selected -> model action

probabilistic_t2.rationale: Do not implement probabilistic T2 yet. First determine whether deterministic T2 survives S1. If it does, uncertainty-aware T2 becomes justified. Otherwise it would be another confounded architecture change.

strongest_realistic_claim: A semantic relation layer can transform raw evidence into a controller-visible epistemic graph on which dynamic MDSG phase routing retains measurable metareasoning value.
do_not: modify M3, T2, or R1 during I3.12
let A1 and M3/R1 see different relation information
implement probabilistic T2 before S1 is evaluated
let the extractor inspect hidden evidence or oracle fields
